summary: BG2 Ep14, Aug 2024: Gerstner explains cutting equity risk from 9 to 3 units as skew deteriorated; discusses recession signals, Fed cuts, AI capex vs revenue, yen carry unwind, Google ruling, gen-AI engagement data and AI take-under deals.

coverage.note: Market sell-off context, public vs private markets
Units of risk framework, Jan 2023 vs mid-2024 skew
Cutting exposure, price vs numbers, five forces list
Uncertainty and multiples, tax cuts and election odds, oil shock
Tax stimulus, soft-landing odds, Wayfair
Consumer slowing, revenue beats, Sahm rule, Fed restrictiveness
Rate-cut pricing, Goolsbee, emergency cut, Fed not thermostat
Cuts before recessions are sold, 2001, markets doing Fed's job
Bubble definition, hyperscaler capex, Nvidia consensus
Hardware cycles, supply vs demand, incumbents moving fast
Incumbent pushback, take-unders, cash use, applied AI
Capex vs revenue in platform shifts, Japan crash set-up
Yen carry trade mechanics and BoJ reversal
Tail risks, geopolitics, giving back YTD, reflexive selling
Do less when prices high; Google ruling
Google ruling economics and remedy
Monopoly test, remedy, Perplexity RAG
Gen-AI engagement and retention data
Personal agent, Google assets, pricing
Google execution, take-under rationale
Take-under structure, regulatory avoidance, taxes
Regulation of small acquisitions; outro

completeness_estimate: 0.93 - first reader covered the risk-sizing framework, macro indicators, Fed, AI capex and carry trade densely; missed a few indicator mentions (JOLTS, delinquencies/defaults), crypto correlation in sell-offs and Gurley's dissent on the carry unwind; three speaker attribution errors.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: stocks are up 60% I mean that's a huge move in six quarters
claims.claim: After a 60% gain in six quarters (QQQ up nearly 80% at peak), a roughly 8% S&P drop is a healthy consolidation, not a 1987-style crash.
claims.indicator: S&P 500 and QQQ drawdown vs six-quarter gain
claims.testable: partly - drawdown depth after rallies testable

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the public markets are the buyers of private companies and you got to know them
claims.claim: Public market valuations and appetite set exit prices for private companies, so venture investors must follow public markets.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: in the public markets we have to think about risk reward every day
claims.claim: A public-markets manager rechecks risk-reward daily, as price rises can come with deteriorating conditions, even while holding a longer horizon in venture.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: when the skew gets more negative when cards get turned over when our probabilities of winning uh dissipate we got to we got to reduce the BET size
claims.claim: Size the net market exposure (units of risk) by the skew of expected outcomes, cutting it when the payoff skew worsens, like bet-sizing in poker.
claims.direction: reduce net long when skew negative

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we said hey we think there's an 80% chance that the names that we like in technology can be up a lot because we expected big earnings beats so up 50%
claims.claim: In January 2023, after low prices, depressed consensus and expected rate cuts, he saw an 80% chance of +50% versus a 20% chance of -10%, a 4-5:1 reward-risk skew, and ran 9 units of risk (about 90-95% net long).
claims.conditions: Low prices, beaten-down expectations, rate cuts ahead

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: now there's an 80% chance that we could have a 20 you know 10 to 20% downside right
claims.claim: By mid-2024 the same framework flipped: prices at all-time highs, in-line earnings, a binary election with tax risk, recession signs and an AI air pocket gave an 80% chance of 10-20% downside, so net exposure was cut.
claims.conditions: Prices parabolic, expectations in line with consensus

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we started to see our earnings expectations which were just line with consensus or in some cases we expected misses to occur
claims.claim: When estimates stop rising above consensus, upside is limited because price has already risen.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: means we sell some of our Longs or we put edges on or we add to our short positions so that our net exposure directionally to the market right is three units of risk
claims.claim: Cutting from 9 to 3 units of risk is done by selling longs, adding hedges or adding shorts, not by exiting the market.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we hold things about three years in the public markets obviously in the Venture markets we're holding things 10 years but that doesn't mean that you buy and go to sleep
claims.claim: Long holding periods (about 3 years public, 10 years venture) are combined with continuous monitoring and resizing when risk-reward changes.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I hear people say um oh my God SAS is super cheap at six times revenue and I'm like you know I've work I've seen Industries mature where where six ain't a stopping point
claims.claim: Valuation anchors from two years ago can mislead: software at six times revenue may not be cheap, and mature industries move to earnings and cash-flow multiples.
claims.conditions: After a 33% Nasdaq rise from January to July

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: as price goes up mathematically risk reward gets worse right unless we're taking up our numbers
claims.claim: Rising price lowers risk-reward unless earnings estimates rise; in 2024 estimates stopped rising materially, so price mattered more.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: depending upon who wins the election we have the potential of an automatic tax increase in 2025
claims.claim: The expiration of Trump personal income tax cuts in 2025 is a potential automatic tax increase, which is the first of five pressure forces (taxes, earnings misses/slowing, AI air pocket, Japan carry unwind, Middle East).
claims.indicator: expiry of TCJA personal tax cuts

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: when that uncertainty goes up the discount rate the margin of safety you need on your portfolio goes up and that means that the multiples on these stocks come down
claims.claim: Higher uncertainty raises the required margin of safety and discount rate, compressing equity multiples.
claims.testable: partly - uncertainty indices vs multiples testable

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it's a it's worth about $150 billion a year to put it in perspective right that's about 60 basis points on US GDP
claims.claim: Expiring individual tax cuts (child tax credit, standard deduction) are worth about $150bn a year, around 60bp of GDP, and a tax increase of that size would be a consumer headwind; corporate cuts are permanent so need Congress.
claims.indicator: US individual tax cuts ($150bn per year, 0.6% of GDP)

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: as the probability of her winning has gone up the market has gotten more concerned about these tax
claims.claim: Betting-market odds of a Harris win rose and the market grew more worried about tax increases; some estimate the Trump tax cuts contributed about 20% of S&P gains.
claims.indicator: election betting odds; tax cut share of S&P gains

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: it could cause an oil shock and that can impact oil prices which obviously has a huge impact on the economy
claims.claim: Escalation with Iran matters for US markets mainly through an oil price shock that hits the economy.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: whatever incremental uh you know take-home pay they got as a result of these tax cuts is being spent
claims.claim: Most recipients of tax cuts have exhausted COVID stimulus and rely on credit, so extra take-home pay is spent, making the cut stimulative; ultra-wealthy are less affected.
claims.indicator: marginal propensity to consume of tax-cut recipients

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: there was an 80% chance of a soft Landing
claims.claim: Markets in July priced about an 80% chance of a soft landing, whereas Jamie Dimon was at 30-35%; the market started repricing toward Dimon's view.
claims.testable: partly - market-implied odds are an approximation

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: customers remain cautious in their spending on the home and our credit card data suggest that the category correction now mirrors the magnitude of the peak to trough decline the Home Furnishing space experienced during the great financial crisis
claims.claim: Wayfair's CEO said home furnishing demand has fallen as much as in the GFC, an early consumer-weakness signal from a housing-sensitive company.
claims.indicator: Wayfair company commentary; home furnishing demand
claims.conditions: Housing under pressure from high rates

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the first thing they do is you know when things are starting to get tight is you defer your couch and that's what Wayfare seeing the second thing you do is you defer your family trip
claims.claim: A consumer squeeze appears first in big-ticket durables (furniture), then in travel and leisure (Airbnb, Disney, cruises, airlines), so weakness in travel confirms broad consumer pressure.
claims.testable: partly - sequence testable with spending data

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: 80% of companies have now reported 48% of them had a positive Revenue beat now that sounds like a lot but it's the lowest level since the third quarter of 2019
claims.claim: Only 48% of S&P companies beat revenue, the lowest since Q3 2019, signalling slowing demand (though it is a trailing indicator).
claims.indicator: share of S&P companies beating revenue estimates

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: a recession is almost always underway if the three-month average unemployment rate Rises by half a percentage point from its low of the past year
claims.claim: The Sahm rule: a recession is almost always underway when the 3-month average unemployment rate rises 0.5pt from its prior 12-month low; it was triggered at 4.3%.
claims.indicator: Sahm rule (3-month avg unemployment vs 12-month low)

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the FED has caused 10 of the last eight recessions
claims.claim: The Fed has often been late, so it may again be late to cut and avoid recession (it was late to raise rates in June 2021).

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it's currently at 1.8% and 50 basis points is viewed as neutral
claims.claim: The 10-year TIPS yield at 1.8% versus a neutral about 0.5%, with fed funds at 5.5% versus a 10-year at 4%, shows the Fed at a multi-decade high in restrictiveness.
claims.indicator: 10-year TIPS real yield vs neutral; fed funds minus 10-year
claims.testable: yes - real yield vs neutral measurable

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we're going to have 125 basis points to 150 basis points of rate Cuts over the course of the next four to five months now to put this in perspective bill that just gets us back to neutral
claims.claim: Market-priced cuts of 125-150bp over four to five months merely return policy to neutral and are not a recession signal.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the real fed funds rate is at its peak for this cycle and we should only have that restrictiveness in place if there's a fear of overheating and the data is weakening
claims.claim: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee: with real rates at the cycle peak, no overheating risk and weakening data, policy restrictiveness is unjustified; inflation concern gives way to jobs.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: that would probably spook the market uh worse than if they just stay the course here um because that would suggest the economy is falling off a cliff
claims.claim: An emergency 75bp cut would signal panic and could hurt markets more than a scheduled cut, since the signal outweighs the action.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the world starts talking about it like it's a thermostat
claims.claim: The Fed is not a thermostat; many other variables (debt, isolationism and de-globalisation inflation, deficits) determine markets, and markets were once addicted to rate cuts as bailouts.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: about a recession are often times sold right it doesn't cause the market to go up actually causes the market to go down
claims.claim: Rate cuts made because of recession fear are often sold: markets fell after the Fed cut in early 2019 and again in 2001, so cuts do not by themselves protect equities.
claims.indicator: equity returns after cuts driven by recession fear
claims.conditions: When cuts react to weak growth rather than lower inflation
claims.testable: yes - event study of cutting cycles

correction.issue: Wrong speaker: the point that cuts made out of recession fear are often sold, with the 2019 data 'our team was looking at', is Brad Gerstner continuing after Gurley's thermostat remark, not Bill Gurley.
correction.fix: Speaker: Brad Gerstner. Rate cuts made because of recession fear are often sold: markets fell after the Fed began cutting in 2019 and again in 2001, so cuts do not by themselves protect equities.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: they were late the game by the time they started cutting rates in the beginning of 2001 it was clear they were behind that the economy was cascading into a recession and the NASDAQ was down over 20%
claims.claim: In 2001 the Fed was behind the curve, started cutting after the dot-com bubble burst, and Nasdaq fell over 20% despite cuts.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: I think the Market's already doing the fed's job right remember that a lot
claims.claim: Long yields have already fallen, lowering mortgage and variable-rate costs, so further Fed cuts have limited marginal effect; economic growth, unemployment and CPI matter more for year-end direction.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the Clinton Administration actually lowered capital gains tax rates which fed into that problem
claims.claim: A cut in capital gains tax rates in the late 1990s added to the dot-com bubble when it should have been raised.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: what a bubble is made of is when everybody believes when there's no talk about an air pocket and when stocks just you know Elevate to ridiculous multiples
claims.claim: A bubble requires universal belief, no worry about an air pocket and ridiculous multiples; since the AI air-pocket talk exists and Nvidia fell from 140 to about 100, this is a healthy consolidation.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: Sundar said it's more dangerous to underspend than to overspend
claims.claim: The four hyperscalers plan about $220bn of capex this year and say under-investing is the bigger risk, so near-term AI demand for Nvidia is supported.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: they're expected to do about 136 billion of data center revenues next year that goes to 166 billion
claims.claim: Consensus Nvidia data-centre revenue of about $136bn this year and $166bn next year is consistent with big-four capex plans and a $2tn data-centre build-out by 2028, with growth rate slowing.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: if the revenues don't materialize that they don't actually have to build out the data center shells right that they're acquiring they said these are 15year long lived assets
claims.claim: Microsoft and Meta CFOs said they can flex data-centre shell build-outs (15-year assets) if revenue lags, reducing capex downside.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: you had to buy hard drive compy companies when their PE was the highest because that was actually when everyone had the the the worst view possible of their earnings possibilities
claims.claim: In boom-bust hardware cycles (PCs, DRAM, hard drives) the P/E is highest at the trough in earnings, so buying at peak P/E and selling at low P/E worked; supply and demand are out of step.
claims.direction: long at high P/E, sell at low P/E
claims.testable: yes - P/E vs forward returns in cyclical sectors

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: whenever you have this kind of really long cycle time to actually bring up incremental capacity it's easier to miss supply and demand
claims.claim: Long lead times for data-centre capacity (land, electricians, power) make supply-demand mismatch more likely, so a capacity overshoot is a risk.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: because everyone the end user is buying these things as a cloud service right I kind of like well that's Supply that's not demand
claims.claim: Nvidia's data-centre growth is mostly supply built by cloud providers and not end-user demand; real demand is the cloud customers' usage.
claims.indicator: Nvidia data-centre revenue vs end-user demand

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: this is one of the very first waves where the incumbents were eyes wide open at the beginning of the technology shift
claims.claim: Unlike past tech shifts, incumbents (Microsoft, Google, Meta) are moving fast in AI, rewarded by the market, so they will keep spending.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: incumbents are aware that if companies get breakout potential they can raise unlimited capital and so to a certain extent I think they're pushing back
claims.claim: Incumbents may spend aggressively (open-source Llama) partly to make it harder for OpenAI and Anthropic to raise the capital for the next model builds; this is Gurley's conjecture.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it is a capitulation no matter what like even if even if it were a normal m&a deal and it was at three billion it's still a great return for investors
claims.claim: AI startup take-under deals (Inflection, Character) signal that independents cannot fund the compute race against incumbents with huge cash flows.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: three things you can do Bill you can buy your own stock you can issue a dividend or you can buy Nvidia chips
claims.claim: With big cash balances and the FTC blocking acquisitions, hyperscalers can only buy back stock, pay dividends or buy Nvidia chips, supporting AI capex.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: all the core AI um opportunities non llm where they've actually figured out how to um go from A to B and get better at what you're doing through AI those are fantastic
claims.claim: Non-LLM applied AI, such as Tesla full self-driving, has clear value, while language-based customer service and search products are less proven.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: in the case of the internet capex got way out ahead of early revenues in the case of cloud capex ahead of early revenues mobile same thing
claims.claim: In prior platform shifts (internet, cloud, mobile) capex ran ahead of revenue, and each super cycle was underestimated over 3-5 years, so a revenue lag does not imply AI capex is wrong.
claims.indicator: capex vs revenue in platform shifts

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I don't think this replaces all software
claims.claim: Statements that AI replaces all software or the new operating system are hyperbole without proof; Gurley sees real use cases but cognitive dissonance in claims.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the Japanese markets were really crowded bill um they hit an all-time high just three weeks ago high prices always make for big drops
claims.claim: The Nikkei was crowded and at a record high, so the BoJ's first hike in 17 years triggered its biggest one-day drop since 1987 (about 13%), followed by a rebound.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: when you have negative rates I.E you're paying somebody to borrow money that leads to what is called a carry trade
claims.claim: Years of negative Japanese rates created a yen carry trade (borrow in yen, buy higher-yielding assets) estimated at over $20tn, which requires predictable BoJ policy.
claims.indicator: yen carry trade; Japan policy rate
claims.testable: yes - carry returns and positioning measurable

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: in the first two days half of those trades they estimated got Unwound that means they had to sell us bonds they had to sell stocks around the world
claims.claim: A surprise BoJ hike forced unwinding of about half of the yen carry trades in two days (JPMorgan estimate), requiring sales of US bonds and global stocks, which feeds negative reflexivity when recession worries already exist.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the US has kept rates higher for longer so it increases the spread there at zero or negative and our rates have been higher for longer so that's LED even more people to Pig pile into this carry trade
claims.claim: A wide US-Japan rate spread (US higher for longer) pushed more capital into the yen carry trade, enlarging the later unwind.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: within 36 hours right it seems like the bank of Japan capitulated and overnight they reversed course
claims.claim: The BoJ reversed within 36 hours, saying it will not raise rates when markets are unstable, and the Nasdaq (QQQ) round-tripped from 475 to 450 and back; it was a long-tail event that can trigger a fuse when other risks exist.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: when markets are at alltime highs and you're just hanging out and there's not a lot of upside return and you got these other things you're concerned about you got to take down those units of risk
claims.claim: At all-time highs with limited upside, tail risks (assassination attempt, geopolitics) justify cutting exposure because rare shocks can hit anytime.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: when the market Market get concerned about it it's generally a buying opportunity because they are generally shortlived
claims.claim: Iran-Israel skirmishes have been short-lived, so geopolitical sell-offs are usually buying opportunities, though a tail where it is different cannot be ruled out.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: this Market could give up a 100% of the gains that we've had year to date which would mean you still have another you'd still have another 10 to 15% down in the market
claims.claim: The market could give back all 2024 gains (10-15% lower) since the world is not clearly better than on January 1, so he saw further downside.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: you got your finger on the sell button and then you wake up and you see this and said I should have sold last week and you start pressing sell right it like it becomes self-reinforcing
claims.claim: When investors are already nervous, a shock triggers self-reinforcing selling (reflexivity), turning moderate news into a sharp market drop.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: when prices are high in the public markets you don't necessarily step out of the markets altogether but you just do less
claims.claim: When prices are high, reduce units of risk rather than exit; the recession risk is the most important of the risks.

correction.issue: Merges two speakers: 'do less, not exit, when prices are high' is Brad Gerstner; the statement that recession is the risk that matters most is Bill Gurley agreeing.
correction.fix: Brad Gerstner: when prices are high, reduce units of risk rather than exit the market; Bill Gurley adds that of the listed risks, recession matters most going forward.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: Google used unfair tactics unfair tactics to maintain itself as the the default search engine on the iPhone over the last decade
claims.claim: A US court found Google illegally maintained its monopoly via the roughly $25bn per year Apple default deal; remedies are to be decided in September.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: whatever the share is that Google's giving to Apple let's say it's 30% or 40% who know it might be 50 you know it represents this massive amount of net income for Apple
claims.claim: The Google payment is a major income stream for Apple (about $26bn), and no competitor such as Bing can replace it, so the deal is win-win not a block.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I think the consumers are going to choose 80 or 90% Google
claims.claim: Remedy of consumer-choice screens would likely leave Google with 80-90% share, so the ruling may be a nothing burger, even better for Google if Apple is cut out.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I've often thought that should be a test for a monopoly like are they able to negotiate deals that are um there they would just be off the table with any other set of Partners
claims.claim: Gurley proposes a monopoly test: whether a firm can impose one-sided terms no other partner could, which would extend its monopoly under Sherman section 2.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: I think the remedy is going to result in Google still getting 90% of the searches
claims.claim: Brad expects consumer choice remedy with Google keeping 90% of searches unless AI products such as Perplexity and SearchGPT disrupt.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: take the results of that search and stuff it through rag into the into the context window and make it part of the prompt
claims.claim: Perplexity and SearchGPT run a search first and feed results into the LLM context (RAG), solving the freshness problem of models and explaining why they show links.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: if you look at these generative AI apps character tops out at about 64% but if you look at Claude Gemini chat GPT they're about 40% so much lower engagement
claims.claim: Weekly-to-monthly active user ratio for ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini is about 40% versus over 80% for Spotify, Instagram and WhatsApp, and apps with over 80% engagement reach billions of users while low-engagement apps cap at tens or 100 million.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: chat GPT it's the best of the Gen apps at about 65% but you see that these generated a AI apps also have not only lower engagement but they have lower retention
claims.claim: One-month retention is about 65% for ChatGPT vs over 90% for WhatsApp, Instagram and Chrome, and 75% for Gmail, so gen-AI apps retain worse (Gurley notes paid and unpaid are mixed).

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it hasn't led to massive Shar shift and it hasn't led to a step function in engagement retention and usage
claims.claim: Because Google copied AI search quickly and engagement is flat, AI chat search is not the product that reaches a billion users.
claims.indicator: ChatGPT engagement, retention, minutes per week

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: maybe the moment is when we all have a personalized agent that has memory about us that can track us over time that really understands us that can take actions
claims.claim: The next breakout AI moment is likely a personalised agent with memory that can act, not AI-enabled search.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the disruptor um just doesn't make as much money and therefore that puts pressure on the incumbent
claims.claim: If free AI search with fewer ads becomes competitive, the disruptor earns less, but incumbents' margin is also pressured; and 12-month retention of about 35% is low.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: it's the best set of assets like if you could pull it all together
claims.claim: Google has the best asset set for a personal assistant (Gmail, docs, Android, workspace) if it integrates them, putting it at an advantage in agents.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it's called execution and Google's been fumbling the ball
claims.claim: Google's main risk in AI is execution, and the current consumer AI product is not enough to dislodge Google search.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: he's looking at the daunting amount of capex required right to continue to compete with meta and continue to compete with Google
claims.claim: Independent model builders face a compute-capex burden, while Google, Microsoft and Meta cannot acquire due to regulation but can pay for talent, leading to licence-and-hire take-under deals.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: we said the most outcome is that they're going to be a seller to Google or to or to or to meta
claims.claim: Gurley's venture firm declined to underwrite Character AI because the likely outcome was a sale to Google or Meta, since breakout was very hard.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker: Brad Gerstner (Altimeter) said 'we looked at both inflection and character' and found Character hard to underwrite, not Bill Gurley, who says he is not in either deal.
correction.fix: Speaker: Brad Gerstner. His firm liked Character AI but found it hard to underwrite because the most likely outcome was a sale to Google or Meta, since breaking out independently was very hard.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: is precisely to avoid um Federal regulatory scrutiny
claims.claim: Non-standard acquihire/licence deals are primarily to avoid federal merger scrutiny, plus double-taxation risk exists, and regulators may close the loophole later.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we need to get back to a place where you know uh Microsoft and Google can go buy you know a company that's Dom Minimus relative to their size
claims.claim: The restrictive acquisition environment forces legal gymnastics; Brad hopes the next administration permits small acquisitions while policing true monopolies.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: you hope for the the you hope for it to be uncorrelated and then oh it's correlated
claims.claim: Crypto, hoped to be a diversifier, fell with equities in the August 2024 sell-off: assets marketed as uncorrelated tend to become correlated in risk-off episodes.
claims.indicator: crypto vs equity correlation in sell-offs
claims.testable: yes - conditional correlation of crypto and equities in drawdowns

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: our jobs report have come in Weak uh the jolts which is the job openings are below Trend um and that trend has been in place for quite a while
claims.claim: Weak payroll reports and job openings (JOLTS) running below trend for an extended period are signs the labour market, and so the economy, is slowing.
claims.indicator: nonfarm payrolls; JOLTS job openings vs trend
claims.testable: yes - JOLTS and payroll series are public

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: consumer delinquencies are rising small business defaults are rising they are at worrisome levels
claims.claim: Citing Goolsbee, rising consumer delinquencies and small-business defaults are forward-looking cautionary indicators of recession even before the data show one.
claims.indicator: consumer loan delinquencies; small business default rates
claims.direction: recession risk up; supports Fed cuts
claims.conditions: while real policy rate is at its cycle peak
claims.testable: yes - delinquency and default series are public

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: at the end of the day it really shouldn't matter for for American investors right this was a Arbitrage thing that had been created by a systematic you know problem in Japan
claims.claim: The yen carry unwind was an arbitrage created by Japan's own policy problem (the BoJ hiked to defend a weak currency), so fundamentally it should not matter for US investors; it mattered only because nervous markets amplified it.
claims.conditions: fundamental impact small unless sentiment is already fragile
claims.testable: partly - could compare US fundamentals vs price move after carry unwinds
